White Plains UMC|Cary._why: Church's own site (313 SE Maynard Rd); feed has no URL. Audit 2026-11-10

504 W. Chapel Hill Street
Durham, NC 27701 (919) 683-3467
_if.access: Those seeking assistance must be Durham County residents and have not received financial assistance from Duke Memorial in the past twelve months.; Requests are taken by phone, (919) 683-3467, or in-person on the first Monday of the month. If the first Monday is a holiday, requests will be taken the following week. Call (919) 683-3467 for the most up-to-date information.

Duke Memorial UMC Good Samaritan Fund|D.name: Duke Memorial UMC Good Samaritan Fund
Duke Memorial UMC Good Samaritan Fund|D.description: Help paying utility bills for Durham County residents, plus free food at a Mobile Market on the third Saturday of each month.
Duke Memorial UMC Good Samaritan Fund|D.address: 504 W. Chapel Hill St, Durham, NC 27701
Duke Memorial UMC Good Samaritan Fund|D.access: Utility help: apply online through the website. Applications are closed until Dec 1 (as of Nov 2026). Must live in Durham County and not have received financial help from Duke Memorial in the past 12 months. Mobile Market: the line usually forms at 7:30am and food is given out at 10am. Call (919) 683-3467 for the latest information.

AIDS Community Residence Association, In.notes: Rent is 30% of adjusted gross income.

Durham Housing Authority (DHA)|Durham.notes: Rent is usually set at about 30% of household income.

El Pueblo- Familias Seguras|Triangle-wid._why: Cost checked 2026-11-10: https://elpueblo.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Guia-de-Emergencia-web.pdf Checked 2026-11-10: The Familias Seguras page describes it as a guide 'designed to help immigrant families in North Carolina prepare for emergencies', available as English and Spanish PDFs. It is not a service. The listed URL pointed straight to the Spanish PDF with tracking parameters. I kept it as a free resource but relabeled it as a guide. https://elpueblo.org/familias-seguras/

_if.description: Know Your Rights Information – NC Resources

El Pueblo- Familias Seguras|Triangle-wid.name: El Pueblo – Familias Seguras (Safe Families) Emergency Guide
El Pueblo- Familias Seguras|Triangle-wid.description: Free guide to help immigrant families in NC prepare for emergencies: know your rights, making a family plan, powers of attorney, getting an ID, and finding legal help. In English and Spanish. This is a guide, not a direct service.
El Pueblo- Familias Seguras|Triangle-wid.access: Read online or download the PDF from the website. Questions: call El Pueblo at (919) 835-1525.
El Pueblo- Familias Seguras|Triangle-wid.notes: El Pueblo also posts recorded know-your-rights webinars on YouTube.

U.S. Committee for Refugees and Immigran.notes: Nominal fees apply; ask about the consultation fee when you contact the hotline.

Council on Immigrant Relations (CIR)|Ral.notes: Low-cost legal help with a nominal consultation fee; payment plans available for representation.

Centro para familias Hispanas|Raleigh.notes: Tax preparation is free; immigration legal consultations cost $50.

Immigrant Solidarity Fund - CWS Durham|D._why: Cost checked 2026-11-10: https://cwsdurham.org/isf/ Checked 2026-11-10: cwsrdu.org/immigrantsolidarityfund/ redirects to cwsdurham.org and the redirect target 404s. The current page is at cwsdurham.org/isf/. It says average waits are 'currently several months' and lists the Triangle group as covering Durham, Orange, and Wake. https://cwsdurham.org/isf/

_if.access: Cash assistance fund for undocumented immigrants in eligible counties impacted by ICE procedures and/or emergency and disaster situations. (assistance is issued based on eligiblity and availibility of funds). Contact Madison Burke for additional information. 919. 641.7825 or immigrantsolidarityfund@cwsglobal.org

Immigrant Solidarity Fund - CWS Durham|D.name: NC Immigrant Solidarity Fund – CWS Durham
Immigrant Solidarity Fund - CWS Durham|D.description: One-time cash grants for immigrant families, regardless of status, to pay for a lawyer or household costs after a family member is arrested by ICE, or when they are otherwise affected by ICE activity.
Immigrant Solidarity Fund - CWS Durham|D.access: For Durham, Orange, and Wake counties (other NC regions have their own groups). Apply with the English or Spanish application on the website, or call or text 919-641-7825. Waitlist is several months as of Nov 2026; applicants are contacted in the order they joined. CWS offices are by appointment only.

WakeTech Community College (ESL)|Raleigh._why: Cost checked 2026-11-10: https://www.waketech.edu/programs-courses/non-credit/strengthen-basic-skills/esl Checked 2026-11-10: The flag was wrong. I replaced the named contact (Tyler Richie, 919-307-9304), which I couldn't find anywhere on Wake Tech's site, with the college's main number, and updated the enrollment steps. https://www.waketech.edu/programs-courses/non-credit/strengthen-basic-skills/esl/esl

_if.access: Contact: Tyler Richie | ELT Instructional Coordinator | tarichie@waketech.edu | 919.307.9304

WakeTech Community College (ESL)|Raleigh.description: English (ESL) classes for adult non-native English speakers who live in Wake County, focused on job readiness. In person and online (online only for students who place at Level 2 or higher).
WakeTech Community College (ESL)|Raleigh.access: Fill out the ESL Interest Form on the website. It is the required first step but does not enroll you. Seats are limited and in high demand, and your English level is assessed at registration. Not for F-1 or J-1 visa holders. Ages 16–17 need extra paperwork.

St Thomas Moore Church|Chapel Hill._why: Cost checked 2026-11-10: https://5520.sites.ecatholic.com/financial-assistance-ministry Checked 2026-11-10: The parish's Financial Assistance Ministry page says it helps Chapel Hill/Carrboro residents with a utility disconnect notice once every 12 months, and 'We do not provide rental assistance.' The ministry line is 919-942-6216, Monday 8:30–11:30am. 919-942-1040 is the parish office. stmchapelhill.org returns 403. I read the ministry page through search results because a direct fetch also returned 403. https://5520.sites.ecatholic.com/financial-assistance-ministry
St Thomas Moore Church|Chapel Hill.name: St. Thomas More Catholic Church – Financial Assistance Ministry
St Thomas Moore Church|Chapel Hill.description: Help paying a utility bill for Chapel Hill and Carrboro residents who have a disconnect notice, once every 12 months. Does not provide rental assistance.
St Thomas Moore Church|Chapel Hill.access: Call Monday mornings 8:30–11:30am and leave a message; messages left at other times are not returned. No walk-ins or email requests.

Self-Help|Durham.notes: Financial coaching is free for members; loans and credit-builder products charge interest.

LIFE House of Durham|Durham.notes: Rent is based on income through project-based Section 8.

CWS Immigration Legal Services Center, D.notes: Legal services are free or low cost; call 919-680-3585 for fees.

North Carolina Justice Center, Raleigh|R._why: Cost checked 2026-11-10: https://www.ncjustice.org/getting-legal-assistance/ Checked 2026-11-10: The intake page says: 'At this time, we are not accepting new cases. We anticipate reopening our intake process in September.' No year is given. https://www.ncjustice.org/getting-legal-assistance/
North Carolina Justice Center, Raleigh|R.description: Free civil and immigration legal help for people with low incomes. Immigration help (asylum, family-based immigration, deportation defense) is available regardless of status. Civil help covers housing, consumer, workers' rights, and public benefits. Does not take criminal, family law, personal injury, or workers' comp cases. Interpreters are available.
North Carolina Justice Center, Raleigh|R.access: Not taking new cases as of Nov 2026; the website says intake should reopen in September. No walk-ins. Legal intake line: 919-856-2162. Spanish immigration line: 1-888-251-2776 (Tue 9am–1pm).
North Carolina Justice Center, Raleigh|R.notes: Check the website or call before applying. Other free legal aid options are listed on its Getting Legal Assistance page.

Asylum Seekers Advocacy Project|Triangle.name: Asylum Seeker Advocacy Project (ASAP)
Asylum Seekers Advocacy Project|Triangle.description: National online membership group for asylum seekers. Offers immigration news and alerts, plus guides and videos on asylum applications, immigration court, USCIS, and work permits. Available in English, Spanish, Haitian Creole, Russian, and Chinese.
Asylum Seekers Advocacy Project|Triangle.access: Online only. Join through the website. Its 'Find Help' page lists legal help referrals.

InStepp Inc|Durham.notes: Low-cost fees for immigration and naturalization help; call 919-680-8000 for prices.

Apex Immigration Services|Apex.notes: Low legal fees on a sliding scale based on ability to pay.

Alliance Medical Ministry|Raleigh.notes: Annual membership of $40–$160 based on household size and income.

Haven House Outreach Center|Raleigh._why: Cost checked 2026-11-10: https://www.hillsboroughstreet.org/go/wrenn-house Checked 2026-11-10: Haven House's site lists no Outreach Center or drop-in center, and no shelter for ages 18+. It lists Street Outreach, Coordinated Entry intake for ages 18–24 (919-980-2015), Transition in Place, and Wrenn House (already a separate listing). 1008 Bullard Ct and 919-833-3312 are the main office. https://www.havenhousenc.org/help/
Haven House Outreach Center|Raleigh.name: Haven House – Youth Street Outreach & Young Adult Intake
Haven House Outreach Center|Raleigh.description: Help for young people facing homelessness. Street Outreach (ages 16–24) brings basic needs items, case management, safety planning, and 24/7 crisis support, and connects youth to shelter and housing. Haven House is also the Wake County Coordinated Entry site for young adults ages 18–24 experiencing homelessness. It has no shelter for anyone 18 or older; the youth shelter for ages 10–17 is Wrenn House.
Haven House Outreach Center|Raleigh.access: Ages 18–24: call the intake line (919) 980-2015 and leave a message; calls are returned within 48 hours. Main office: (919) 833-3312, info@havenhousenc.org. Transition in Place housing (ages 18–23) is by referral through Street Outreach.
Haven House Outreach Center|Raleigh.notes: The old Haven House Outreach Center drop-in (Wake Forest Rd) is not listed on Haven House's current website.

Volunteers of America and of the Carolin.name: Volunteers of America Chesapeake & Carolinas – Maple Court Veteran Apartments
Volunteers of America and of the Carolin.description: 24 apartments with case management for veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness, run in partnership with the VA. VOA now lists it as permanent housing, not transitional.
Volunteers of America and of the Carolin.access: No referral needed, but you must complete an application before admission interviews with VA and Maple Court staff. Volunteers of America and of the Carolin._why: Checked 2026-11-10: The program still exists. Troy House|Durham.name: STSG Transitional House (Straight Talk Support Group)
Troy House|Durham.description: Transitional housing (usually up to 90 days) for up to 21 justice-involved adult men leaving prison. Offers life skills, financial literacy, technology and job-readiness training, individual and group peer support, family mediation, work-based learning, and NA/AA.
Troy House|Durham.access: Accepts referrals only from reentry programs and correctional institutions, through the referral page on its website. Cannot accept people with arson or sexual offenses. Program manager: (984) 219-1001. Crisis line: (919) 599-5125.
Troy House|Durham.notes: Formerly called The Troy House at 1101 N Mangum St. The group says it now runs from a new site, with no address published (mailing address: PO Box 51654, Durham, NC 27717). Its state funding was cut in March 2024 and it relies on donations, so call to confirm it has space.
Troy House|Durham._why: Checked 2026-11-10: The STSG site calls the program 'STSG Transitional House'. Its homepage says the original house at 1101 N Mangum St 'later became known as The Troy House' and that STSG 'operates from a new site, continuing its mission of providing transitional housing'. ABC11 (Aug 2024) reported the state funding cut and that it might close, but I found no closure notice. The site's newest date is 2023. https://www.straighttalksupportgroup.org/
